what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It combines two medicines in one tablet: olmesartan, which relaxes your blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard, and hydrochlorothiazide (a water pill), which helps your kidneys remove extra salt and water from your body. Together, they help lower your blood pressure and reduce your risk of heart attack and stroke.
how_to_take: Take this tablet by mouth once a day, with or without food. Swallow it whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time every day so you do not forget. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablet unless your doctor or pharmacist tells you it is okay.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your blood pressure and your response to the medicine. Common starting doses are olmesartan 20 mg with hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg once daily. Your doctor may increase your dose over time up to a maximum of olmesartan 40 mg with hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg once daily. Always take the dose your doctor prescribed — do not change it on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep it in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of the reach of children and pets. If you no longer need this medicine, ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid potassium supplements or salt substitutes containing potassium unless your doctor tells you it is okay, as this combination can raise potassium levels too high. Limit alcohol, as it can lower your blood pressure further and cause dizziness or fainting. Avoid getting up too quickly from sitting or lying down, especially when you first start taking this medicine, to prevent dizziness. Be careful in hot weather or during heavy exercise because sweating too much can lead to low blood pressure or dehydration. Avoid NSAIDs (pain relievers like ibuprofen or naproxen) unless approved by your doctor, as they can make this medicine work less well and harm your kidneys.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat (this could be a serious allergic reaction called angioedema); severe dizziness or fainting; signs of high potassium such as muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat, or numbness; signs of low sodium such as headache, confusion, or weakness; decreased urination or signs of kidney problems; severe diarrhea or vomiting and inability to keep fluids down; yellowing of your skin or eyes; vision changes or eye pain (which could signal increased eye pressure); or if you become pregnant. Also call your doctor if your blood pressure does not seem to be getting better.
when_it_works: You may start to see your blood pressure lower within the first 1 to 2 weeks of taking this medicine. The full effect is usually seen within 4 to 8 weeks. Even if you feel well and notice no symptoms, it is very important to keep taking this medicine every day. High blood pressure often has no symptoms, but if left untreated it can cause serious problems like heart attack, stroke, or kidney damage.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT take this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby, especially during the second and third trimesters. Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding, as this medicine may pass into breast milk. Children: This medicine is not typically recommended for children. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to dizziness and low blood pressure — rise slowly from sitting or lying positions. Kidney or liver disease: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted or this medicine may not be right for you. Diabetes: The hydrochlorothiazide component may affect your blood sugar levels, so monitor them closely and tell your doctor.
